“New York is an ugly city, a dirty city. Its climate is a scandal, its politics are used to frighten children, its traffic is madness, its competition is murderous. But there is one thing about it: once you have lived in New York and it has become your home, no place else is good enough.”

-John Steinbeck

i moved to New York City because i am in love with the energy, essence and resilience that makes this city feel so alive and exciting that it has literally earned the name ‘the center of the world’.

The past 24 hours have been so remarkably morbid here and you can feel the fear and confusion in the air. The streets are quiet. Everyone is masked, and those who aren’t are visibly on edge. This virus has turned the ‘city that never sleeps’ into a dark and scary frontier, and has sucked so much of the essence that makes it special away.

NYC is an absurd social experiment, and the exact things that made it special and important culturally are the things that have created the conditions which make new yorkers so much more vulnerable to infection .

Eventually, this disaster will subside and the magic of the 5 boroughs will return. But please take a few minutes to think about the importance of taking any possible preventable measures and brace yourself for the reality of this virus spreading across  the country and the potential loss of life it will be responsible for.

There are a lot of unknown outcomes right now, and the severity of those outcomes are far more devastating than we have been faced with in centuries. Nobody knows the economic impact or the psychological trauma that could be collectively felt.

But the one thing i know is that New York City will survive this and continue to be a beacon of humanity, the nucleus of American culture and trends and an unthinkable accomplishment of civilization...a place where nothing is impossible and the most important metropolitan achievement ever conceived

It may seem to be a bleak or boring mindset, but 100% of the evidence corroborates it and every day we become more competent in understanding the minutiae of how it all works.
